title: High throughput application of ASTM D8332 for microplastic sampling in riverine systems
author: Bryksa, McGlashan, et al.

steps.title: Choose pump and verify specifications
steps.instruction: Use the Jabsco 12 V DC freshwater centrifugal pump (compatible with a 12 V battery, minimal plastic components, capable of pumping large water volumes and solid particles).

steps.title: Assemble stainless‑steel plumbing
steps.instruction: Connect ¾‑inch (OD) stainless‑steel tubing using 4‑foot sections and compression fittings; typically three sections (12 ft total) for surface‑water sampling. Install a 90° elbow at the inlet facing the river flow (add an optional 5 mm mesh screen if debris is high) and a 90° bend at the outlet directing flow onto the sieve stack. Ensure all connections match the pump’s ¾‑inch NPT fittings.

steps.title: Fix inlet and pump orientation
steps.instruction: Secure the river inlet and centrifugal pump with stainless‑steel stakes and clamps. Position the inlet to face the current and the pump on the shore side hovering over the sieve stack. Set the inlet 1–1.5 inches below the water surface to avoid air suction; if air is drawn, return to the priming step.

steps.title: Install battery and protective housing
steps.instruction: Place a 12 V lithium‑iron‑phosphate battery (lightest available) in a waterproof protective case and connect it to power the pump for multiple 1500 L samples.

steps.title: Prime centrifugal pump
steps.instruction: Fill the entire tubing and pump housing with water to create back‑pressure and eliminate air bubbles before starting the pump; the pump must not operate from a dry state.

steps.title: Determine manual flow rate
steps.instruction: Using a calibrated bucket of known volume and a timer, measure the time required to fill the bucket at the start of sampling. Calculate the flow rate (L min⁻¹) and compute the pumping time needed for the desired total volume (usually 1500 L), keeping the final volume within ±5 % of target.

steps.title: Prepare sieve stack and field blank
steps.instruction: Stack ASTM E‑11 sieves on an 8‑inch aluminum table with spiked legs in the order: 5 mm, 500 µm, 125 µm, 45 µm (omit 1 mm and 300 µm sieves that emptied after 1500 L). Place a pre‑cleaned 45 µm blank sieve wrapped in tin foil in the second slot; unwrap and insert it just before sampling begins. Keep a spare 45 µm sieve for replacement if clogging occurs; replace all 45 µm sieves every two months as a precaution.

steps.title: Start water sampling
steps.instruction: Activate the pump for the calculated duration to collect the target volume; water flows from the inlet through the tubing and onto the sieve stack, capturing suspended particles.

steps.title: Monitor for air intake and clogging
steps.instruction: Watch the inlet depth; if air is drawn, stop sampling and repeat the priming step. Observe the sieve stack for clogging; replace or rinse the 45 µm sieve as needed without losing the prime.

steps.title: Rinse sieves after collection
steps.instruction: In the field, rinse each sieve with filtered water from the bottom of the stack into glass containers with aluminum lids using stainless‑steel beakers. After the field day, clean sieves by cycles of sonication and rinsing with filtered type‑2 water. Pre‑rinse sieves with site water before each sampling event and visually inspect for mesh damage.

steps.title: Store equipment
steps.instruction: Disassemble tubing, secure the pump and battery in their waterproof cases, and transport all components in clean containers to avoid contamination.

steps.title: Optional: Use portable doppler flow meter
steps.instruction: If desired, clamp a Greyline PDFM 5.1 portable doppler flow meter externally to the ¾‑inch tubing; calibrate for inner diameter and bend distance to obtain real‑time flow data. Note the higher cost and longer setup time.

steps.title: Discard corrugated tubing (if used)
steps.instruction: Do not use corrugated stainless‑steel tubing; it retains particles and can cause cross‑contamination, so remove it from the final design.
